skeptic.objection: This parcel is not open land: it is part of the land of a named developer's three-building project. The developer applied for the rezoning, sued the city when it was denied, won the M-1 zoning on a court-ordered revote in March 2026, and in April 2026 told the county development authority that the zoning is in hand and the biggest tenant is secured, with a bond inducement of up to $220 million covering all three buildings on the whole assemblage. An outside buyer has no visible way in unless that deal has lapsed. What is not shown is a completed sale: no final bond resolution appears on the authority's agendas through 27 October 2026 and the county parcel record still names the 2012 owner, so a person should check the deed records before dropping the lead for good.

open_items: First question: has anything been recorded against this parcel or its six neighbours since April 2026 (a deed, a memorandum of contract or option, a lease to the development authority)? Check the Fulton County Clerk of Superior Court deed records by hand. If nothing has, ask whether the developer's contract is still live: the authority's estimate of a third-quarter 2026 closing has passed with no final bond resolution on its agendas through 27 October 2026 (its next meetings are listed for 17 November and 1 December 2026).

Dispute of market-4: the 'estimated closing date' in the development authority's release is, on the authority's own fact sheet, a field of the bond inducement. No page read by either pass shows a land purchase contract or its closing date. The quotes show a developer pursuing the land with the owner's land in the project's name, not a contract; the practical result for an outside buyer is the same.

Dispute of utilities-4: the checklist makes the utilities verdict the weaker of water and sewer. Sewer is shown nearby and water is not shown, so the section's verdict should read not_shown, not nearby. Also ask whether the Morning Creek sewer lines found within 1,500 ft can serve a site that the staff report says drains to a tributary of Whitewater Creek, or whether a pump station or an extension is needed.

Dispute of plans-6: the kept quote gives a resolution number and a date and does not say what the moratorium covers. That it concerns data centres and not warehouses rests on the first agent's reading of the rest of the page.

What is the state of the developer's lawsuit against the city (a news report listed it as open on 7 April 2026), and has anyone filed a challenge to ORD2026-010? A rezoning that came from a court-ordered revote is worth a look at the Fulton County Superior Court docket before relying on it.

Seen, not verifiable: https://www.cityofsouthfultonga.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_03242026-1806 pages 7 and 8 are images with no text layer. Page 7 (GRTA Attachment A) asks for Old Senoia Road to be paved as a two-lane road between SR 74 and the site's first driveway and through the rest of the site, with a sidewalk, and for turn lanes on SR 74 and SR 92/Spence Road, all subject to GDOT approval. Page 8 is the zoning site plan, titled with the developer's name and the project name. A buyer of this parcel alone would want to know which of these road works fall on it.

My own arithmetic, not checked by anyone: the Irwin Road courses of the first tract in the legal description add up to about 2,650 ft, close to the brief's 2,525 ft of frontage on one local road, which fits this parcel lying inside the 72.35-acre tract. Condition 1 of the posted ordinance calls the site plan 'conceptual only', so the conditions do not appear to tie the zoning to the three-building layout; that point is in the lead's favour if the land ever comes free.

Not found after searching: any report of a land closing, a land disturbance permit, a groundbreaking or a named tenant for this site after April 2026; any warehouse moratorium or M-1 text amendment by the city since March 2026; any lawsuit filed by residents. Not looked at: deed records, court dockets, the city's permit records, the Secretary of State record, listing sites (never used; a person may look at them by hand).
